name: Pharma / Biotech
tagline: A barbell of risk — from speculative, FDA-binary small-cap biotech (XBI, ARKG) to cash-rich mega-cap pharma (PPH) — in a sector that swings on trial readouts, drug-pricing politics, M&A and rates. Pick your weighting scheme and sub-industry; they behave very differently.
universe_note: Three distinct sub-themes hide under one label: biotech (XBI/IBB), big pharma (PPH), and genomics (ARKG). They are NOT interchangeable. Use 'Add ticker' to pull any fund not listed (e.g. XPH for equal-weight pharma, XLV variants).
key_tensions: FDA binary-event risk: small/mid-cap biotech (XBI, ARKG) can move 30-80% on a single trial readout or approval/CRL — idiosyncratic risk that big pharma (PPH) and broad healthcare (XLV) largely dampen.

Equal-weight XBI vs cap-weight IBB: XBI equal-weights ~150 biotechs (top-10 ~15%, heavy small/clinical-stage tilt, high beta); IBB cap-weights ~255 names but is top-heavy (top-10 ~45-50%) dominated by 4 profitable mega-caps. Same sector, very different risk.

Biotech vs pharma vs genomics: biotech = US R&D/commercial biotech; pharma = profitable dividend-paying large caps (often foreign-domiciled ADRs); genomics = a money-losing-heavy thematic basket. Different exposures entirely.
ARKG active concentration: ~33 names, top-10 ~60%, single names up to ~10%, high turnover, brutal drawdowns (-28% in 2024, -54% in 2022) and key-person risk. You're buying a manager's thesis.
PPH is Lilly-dependent: a 25-stock fund with Eli Lilly ~18-19% and top-10 ~71% — closer to a concentrated GLP-1/big-pharma basket than a diversified fund; also thinly traded (~264K shares/day).

Why XLV is a yardstick: it's broad healthcare (insurers, devices, tools + drugmakers), the cheapest (0.08%) and most liquid option — the 'did the concentrated bet actually beat plain healthcare?' reference.
benchmark_note: XLV (broad healthcare) is the yardstick, NOT a pure biotech/pharma bet — a big chunk is insurers (UnitedHealth), devices (Abbott) and tools (Thermo Fisher). Use it to judge whether the concentration and cost of a pure biotech/pharma fund were rewarded vs simply owning the sector cheaply.

etfs.name: SPDR S&P Biotech ETF

performance.note: Total return. Huge 1-yr (+52.7%) off a flat 2024 (+1.0%) — sharp biotech recovery. High historical volatility; prior multi-year drawdowns.

cost.note: 0.35% — typical for a sector ETF, not cheap.

purity.note: ~100% biotech, ~96% US — the cleanest biotech beta.

concentration.note: Equal-weight; top-10 ~15%, no name above ~2% — risk is broad-sector, not single-name.

track_record.note: Long history (2006) but high volatility and past deep drawdowns.

etfs.overall: Cleanest, most liquid pure-biotech beta — high reward, high volatility, low single-name risk.

memo.thesis: XBI is the purest, highest-beta way to own the broad biotech innovation cycle with minimal single-stock risk via equal weighting. It gives small/mid-cap clinical-stage biotech a real seat at the table, so it captures M&A pops and risk-on rallies — but whipsaws hard. The go-to vehicle for 'biotech is recovering'.
memo.strategy: Tracks the S&P Biotechnology Select Industry Index using MODIFIED EQUAL WEIGHTING with periodic rebalancing, so each of ~150 names carries a similar ~0.6-1.8% weight regardless of market cap. This structurally tilts toward smaller, often pre-revenue biotechs and avoids mega-cap domination — producing high rebalance turnover and elevated volatility.

purity_verdict.text: Essentially 100% biotech, ~96%+ US. The cleanest 'biotech beta' of the group.

memo.concentration: Lowest concentration of the group — top-10 only ~14-16%, no single name above ~2%. Risk is broad-sector, not name-specific.
memo.cost_context: 0.35% is standard for a sector/industry ETF — middle of this pack; cheaper than ARKG, far above XLV (0.08%).
memo.track_record_note: Long history since 2006. Strong 2025 (+35.9%) and huge trailing 1-yr (+52.7%) off 2024's flat (+1.0%) year. High historical volatility and prior multi-year drawdowns (2021-23 bear) are the trade-off.
red_flags: ⚠️ Equal weight = persistent small/clinical-stage exposure → high drawdown risk.
⚠️ Very high beta — whipsaws in risk-off / rising-rate regimes.
bull: Best vehicle to capture biotech M&A/innovation broadly

decision_log.text: The clean biotech-beta pick. Equal-weight = lower single-name risk but high volatility — size accordingly. Compare trailing return vs XLV to see if the extra risk paid.

etfs.name: iShares Biotechnology ETF

performance.note: Total return; 1-yr is annualized to Mar 31 2026. Solid 2025 after down 2024; flat-to-negative YTD after a Jan peak. Lower drawdowns than XBI.

cost.note: 0.44% — priciest passive biotech here, notably above XBI's 0.35%.

purity.note: ~100% biotech, mostly US; slightly less innovation-stage than XBI (mega-caps dominate).

concentration.note: High for 255 names — top-10 ~45-50%, four mega-caps ~7% each.

etfs.overall: Steadier, mega-cap-anchored biotech core — but pricey and top-heavy on 4 names.

memo.thesis: IBB is the 'blue-chip biotech' core — cap-weighted toward the four profitable biotech mega-caps (Vertex, Gilead, Amgen, Regeneron), giving steadier exposure than XBI but real top-heaviness. The way to own biotech where earnings and cash flow, not just pipeline lottery tickets, drive most of the return.
memo.strategy: Tracks the NASDAQ Biotechnology Index, cap-weighted, so the largest profitable biotechs dominate while a long tail of ~250 names adds breadth but little weight. Lower turnover and lower volatility than XBI; behaves more like large-cap growth healthcare than speculative biotech.

purity_verdict.text: Pure biotech by classification, predominantly US. Slightly less 'innovation-stage' than XBI because mega-caps dominate.

memo.concentration: High for a 255-name fund — top-10 ~45-50%, four names ~7% each. Idiosyncratic risk concentrated in Vertex/Gilead/Amgen/Regeneron.
memo.sector_geo: Overwhelmingly US biotech; mega-cap led with a small/mid-cap tail.
memo.cost_context: 0.44% is the most expensive passive biotech option here and notably above XBI's 0.35% — a long-standing knock on IBB.
memo.track_record_note: Longest history of the group (2001). Solid 2025 (+28.0%) after a down 2024 (-2.4%); flat-to-slightly-negative YTD 2026 after an early-Jan peak. Lower drawdowns than XBI historically.
red_flags: ⚠️ YTD negative after Jan peak (momentum cooling).
bear: Mega-cap maturity caps upside vs small-cap biotech

decision_log.text: The steadier biotech core. If you want biotech without XBI's whipsaw, IBB works — but you pay 0.44% and ride 4 mega-caps. Verify avg volume before trading.

etfs.name: ARK Genomic Revolution ETF

performance.note: Total return. Extremely volatile: strong 2025 (+23%) & 1-yr (+35.8%) but devastating 2024 (-28%) and 2022 (-54%). High-amplitude vehicle.

cost.note: 0.75% — by far the most expensive here (~2x XBI/IBB, ~9x XLV).

purity.note: On-theme for genomics but mixes diagnostics/tools/'techbio' (Tempus, 10x), not biotech-pure.

concentration.note: ~33 names, top-10 ~60%, top name ~10% — single-stock & thesis risk dominate.

liquidity.note: ~3.5M shares/day — adequate but thinner than XBI/IBB.

track_record.note: Severe drawdowns (-28% in 2024, -54% in 2022); mixed long-run record.

etfs.overall: High-octane active genomics bet — big upside, brutal drawdowns, premium fee, concentrated.

memo.thesis: ARKG is a concentrated, actively managed bet on the genomics revolution — gene editing, molecular diagnostics, genomic tools — NOT a diversified biotech fund. Outsized upside if the thesis plays out, but severe drawdown risk, high fees, and dependence on a few money-losing, high-multiple names.
memo.strategy: Active, high-conviction. ~33-35 names, top-10 ~60%, single positions up to ~10%, spanning gene editing (CRISPR, Beam), diagnostics (Tempus, Personalis) and tools (Twist, 10x, Illumina). Holdings shift frequently with ARK's research views; manager/key-person risk is material.

purity_verdict.text: ~98% healthcare/genomics and on-theme for genomics, but deliberately holds diagnostics, tools and 'techbio' (e.g. Tempus AI) that aren't classic biotech drug developers — a narrower, idiosyncratic slice.

memo.concentration: Highest of the group — ~33 holdings, top-10 ~60%, top name ~10%. Single-stock and thesis risk are dominant.
memo.sector_geo: ~98% healthcare/genomics, ~91% US. Skews small/mid-cap and pre-profit.
memo.cost_context: 0.75% — by far the most expensive of the group (more than 2x XBI/IBB, ~9x XLV). An active-management premium that must be earned through stock selection.
memo.track_record_note: Extremely volatile. Strong 2025 (+23%) and trailing 1-yr (+35.8%), but devastating 2024 (-28%) and 2022 (-54%) — a high-amplitude vehicle whose long-run record is mixed.
bull: Differentiated genomics exposure unavailable in passive funds
bear: Worst drawdown profile of the group
You're buying a manager, not an index

decision_log.text: The aggressive genomics bet. Only for high risk tolerance: 0.75% fee, ~60% top-10, -54% drawdown history. Size small; treat as a manager bet, not index exposure.

etfs.name: VanEck Pharmaceutical ETF

performance.note: Total return. Lower-volatility than biotech, dividend-paying; increasingly Lilly / GLP-1-driven.

cost.note: 0.36% — fair, not cheap, for a 25-stock cap-weighted basket.

purity.note: ~100% pharma — but note pharma≠biotech, and several top names are foreign-domiciled ADRs.

concentration.note: Only 25 names, top-10 ~71%, Eli Lilly alone ~18-19% — extreme single-name dependence.

liquidity.note: ~264K shares/day — thinnest of the group; wider spreads.

etfs.overall: Stable, dividend-paying big-pharma exposure — but dangerously Lilly-dependent and thinly traded.

memo.thesis: PPH is a concentrated, cap-weighted bet on the world's largest BRANDED pharmaceutical companies — profitable, dividend-paying franchises (Lilly, Novartis, Merck, Novo, Pfizer) — the lowest-pipeline-risk, most value/quality-tilted option among the theme funds. Its fortunes ride disproportionately on Eli Lilly (~18-19%) and the GLP-1/obesity cycle.
memo.strategy: Tracks the MVIS US Listed Pharmaceutical 25 Index — just 25 large, US-listed (including foreign-domiciled ADR) pharma names, cap-weighted with caps. Low turnover, dividend income (~2.1% yield), large-cap stability — but deliberately narrow and very top-heavy.

purity_verdict.text: ~100% pharmaceuticals (on-theme), but note (a) it's pharma, NOT biotech — a different sub-industry, and (b) several top names are foreign-domiciled (Novartis, Novo, AstraZeneca) despite 'US Listed' — a global-pharma-via-US-listing bet.

memo.concentration: Very high — only 25 names, top-10 ~71%, Lilly alone ~18-19%. Closer to a concentrated large-cap basket than a diversified fund; Lilly-specific risk is the single biggest factor.
memo.sector_geo: 100% pharma; meaningful foreign-domiciled exposure (Swiss/Danish/UK names) via US listings.
memo.cost_context: 0.36% — in line with XBI (0.35%) and below ARKG; reasonable but not cheap for a 25-stock cap-weighted basket, and well above XLV's 0.08%.
memo.track_record_note: Decent, lower-volatility profile vs biotech: +19.4% (2024), +5.5% (2025), +17.8% YTD 2026, ~+18% trailing 1Y. Returns increasingly Lilly/GLP-1-driven. Pays a ~2.1% dividend.
red_flags: 🚩 Extreme single-name dependence on Eli Lilly (~18-19%).

decision_log.text: The stable big-pharma pick — but it's ~18-19% Eli Lilly and thinly traded. If you want diversified pharma, consider equal-weight XPH (Add ticker); if you want Lilly, you could just buy Lilly.

etfs.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund

performance.note: Benchmark, total return. Steady, low-volatility healthcare. Far smaller drawdowns than biotech. (Note: 2024 +2.5% — an early search wrongly returned XLV's 2019 figure.)

cost.note: 0.08% — cheapest here by a wide margin (~1/4 of the theme funds).

purity.note: Broad healthcare, NOT pure biotech/pharma — big insurer/device/tools weights. Benchmark only.

concentration.note: Top-10 ~60% but diversified ACROSS sub-industries; lower single-name risk than PPH/ARKG.

track_record.note: Long history (1998), low volatility, far smaller drawdowns than biotech.

etfs.overall: Benchmark — cheap, liquid, diversified healthcare core; the reference, not a concentrated bet.

memo.thesis: REFERENCE FUND, NOT A PURE BIOTECH/PHARMA BET. XLV is broad, cap-weighted US large-cap healthcare — pharma + biotech + managed care + devices + tools — at rock-bottom cost. The standard against which the concentrated theme funds should be judged: if XBI/IBB/ARKG/PPH didn't beat XLV after higher fees and risk, the concentrated bet didn't pay.
memo.strategy: Tracks the Health Care Select Sector Index (the ~60-65 healthcare members of the S&P 500), cap-weighted. Diversified across sub-industries, anchored by Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, UnitedHealth, Merck. Low turnover, very high liquidity, minimal fee.

purity_verdict.text: Only a portion is drug developers; large weights are insurers (UnitedHealth), devices (Abbott) and tools (Thermo Fisher). Intentionally NOT a pure theme fund — that's why it's the yardstick.

memo.concentration: Top-10 ~60%, Lilly ~16%, but diversified ACROSS sub-industries; single-name risk lower than PPH/ARKG and spread across healthcare verticals.
memo.sector_geo: US large-cap healthcare, all sub-industries; predominantly domestic.
memo.cost_context: 0.08% — cheapest by a wide margin (~1/4 of the pharma/biotech funds, ~1/9 of ARKG). The cost advantage compounds meaningfully over time.
memo.track_record_note: Steady, low-volatility: +2.5% (2024), +13.3% (2025), ~+16.4% trailing 1Y, ~flat YTD 2026. Long history since 1998; far smaller drawdowns than biotech.
red_flags: ⚠️ Not a pure biotech/pharma bet — big insurer/device weights.
⚠️ Managed-care (UNH) policy/regulatory risk drives part of returns.
⚠️ Will lag in a pure biotech rip.
bear: Less upside in biotech bull runs

decision_log.text: The yardstick. Before buying any concentrated pharma/biotech fund, check whether it beat this cheap, diversified, lower-risk option after fees.
